records.title: PM-JAY → Khyati: claim earnings, clinical allegations and later bail
records.summary: Public health cover reaches a named private hospital. A sessions-court account records ₹16.64 crore in PM-JAY claim earnings and alleges ₹8 crore bank-loan use; patient-level records and bank reconciliation remain absent. The clinical charges are contested. The Supreme Court granted the chairman bail in December 2025; discharge refusals were reported in May 2026.
records.status: Charges contested; chairman granted bail 11 Dec 2025; discharge refusals reported May 2026; no merits verdict retained
records.dateBasis: Dates bound the explicitly described events or reviewed procedural observations; fiscal and transaction periods remain attached to each amount.
records.period: Claims 31 Mar 2022–11 Nov 2024; clinical incident 11 Nov 2024; last retained procedural report 9 May 2026
records.response: Dr Prashant Vazirani’s counsel argued clinical indications and pre-authorisation justified the procedures, complications could explain the deaths, and some patients declined treatment. Kartik Patel’s counsel disputed personal withdrawal and day-to-day management. The Gujarat HC rejected the doctor’s May 2025 bail plea on a prima facie view; the Supreme Court’s 11 Dec 2025 order records later bail for him and all other co-accused and grants Patel bail. A May 2026 report records discharge refusal. No final conviction or acquittal is established.
alternativeExplanations: Legitimate PM-JAY treatment also earns package revenue; the total cannot be classified as fraud without claim-level findings.
A corporate loan repayment can serve hospital operations. It does not establish personal withdrawal or illegality without the source-of-funds and clinical evidence.
Adverse medical outcome alone does not prove unnecessary treatment or criminal intent.
records.falsifier: Obtain authenticated claims adjudication and disbursement ledgers, clinical videos/independent reviews, bank-use tracing and the final reasoned trial or appellate judgment; reconcile each disputed claim and preserve any acquittal or recovery.

amounts.stage: Hospital earnings reported in a sessions-court bail order for 3,578 PM-JAY angiography/angioplasty claims; not independently reconciled bank receipts or proven loss

records.title: Byju’s: a dollar loan, an Indian guarantee and a ₹158 crore escrow
records.summary: The source trail links US lender funding through GLAS to BYJU’S Alpha, Think & Learn’s guarantee and a separate BCCI sponsorship debt. The Supreme Court set aside approval of the ₹158 crore settlement because insolvency-withdrawal procedures were bypassed, while expressly declining a merits finding on stakeholder conduct. The August 2026 NCLAT dismissal also left the underlying creditor dispute open.
records.status: Indian settlement approval set aside; funds protected in escrow by order; August 2026 procedural appeal dismissed, underlying issues left open
records.dateBasis: Dates bound the explicitly described events or reviewed procedural observations; fiscal and transaction periods remain attached to each amount.
records.period: Facility 24 Nov 2021; CIRP admitted 16 Jul 2024; SC 23 Oct 2024; NCLAT 17 Aug 2026
records.response: Riju Ravindran’s undertaking said settlement funds were personal, derived from his share-sale resources, and did not come from the disputed US loan proceeds. GLAS challenged that provenance and priority. The Supreme Court §§86–87 made no finding on stakeholder conduct and left remedies under the proper withdrawal procedure available. In 2026 Byju’s side challenged lender authorisations and claim quantum; NCLAT declined to adjudicate those merits in an appeal from a listing order.
alternativeExplanations: A documented guarantee and operational debt explain a multi-creditor insolvency without themselves proving diversion.
Payment by a third party can be lawful; lawful source and compliance still need proof where challenged.
The US transfer disputes and Indian withdrawal litigation are distinct proceedings; one cannot stand in for a final outcome in the other.
records.falsifier: Produce the relevant authenticated lender authorisations, disbursement/transfer bank records, guarantee enforcement and final merits orders; determine the exact funds used for settlement and any later escrow distribution.

amounts.stage: Contracted term-loan facility to US borrower; guarantor exposure is the same facility, not a second disbursement
Settlement sum held in escrow and ordered transferred to committee-of-creditors escrow; not lender recovery or adjudicated proceeds of fraud

geography.note: Think & Learn’s Bengaluru corporate/insolvency association; not a map of loan deployment or school delivery. US borrower and litigation are separately described.

limitations: Dollar loan principal and rupee operational-debt settlement are different currencies and obligations; never sum them.
No final US recovery or damages number is presented, and no inference about public subsidy or school-delivery outcome is supported.
No current company valuation is supplied merely because the brand was previously described as a unicorn.

records.title: Akshaya Patra: state support, school meals and related-party payments
records.summary: A documented NGO service chain separates state-support income from cash receipts, identifies the Thakkar-funded Chikkajala kitchen and exposes the audited₹275.76 lakh rent/other-expense payment to related party ISKCON Bangalore. The trust reports kitchen coverage; neither charity status nor related-party disclosure establishes misuse. No restricted government grant is traced to a particular rent payment.
records.status: Audited financial disclosures retained; programme delivery is self-reported; no misconduct finding asserted
records.dateBasis: Dates bound the explicitly described events or reviewed procedural observations; fiscal and transaction periods remain attached to each amount.
records.period: FY 2024-25; kitchen inaugurated 30 Sep 2024; audited statements signed 7 Oct 2025
records.response: This is a funding-transparency case, with no fraud allegation asserted. The Foundation’s audited statements disclose the related parties and transaction categories. Walker Chandiok & Co LLP gave an unmodified financial-statement opinion with emphasis on the adopted trust accounting basis. Programme narrative describes school nutrition work; it is not the same assurance as an independent service-outcome audit.
alternativeExplanations: Income and cash receipts differ because of the accounting basis, in-kind support, receivables, provisions and advances. Their difference is not automatically loss.
Related organisations may legitimately share premises and services. Assessing value requires the lease, allocation basis and comparable charges.
A kitchen’s capacity or inauguration promise may exceed period-end children actually served.
records.falsifier: Reconcile government sanctions and bank credits to Schedule B and grain support; match kitchen registers to school acknowledgments; inspect leases, common-trustee approvals, cost allocation and market comparisons before asserting excess or grant misuse.

records.title: NSAP → DAVP: publicity spending and missing work confirmation
records.summary: CAG traced two approved publicity amounts into DAVP work orders, then found₹2.83 crore charged to NSAP for other ministry schemes and paid before confirmation of execution. That documents an earmarking and delivery-verification failure. It does not prove partisan advertising or identify personal enrichment. Later parliamentary material checked here does not close this specific audit paragraph.
records.status: CAG finding with Ministry response; final paragraph-specific reconciliation or recovery not established
records.dateBasis: Dates bound the explicitly described events or reviewed procedural observations; fiscal and transaction periods remain attached to each amount.
records.period: June/August 2017 sanctions; June/September 2017 work orders; December 2022 Ministry response; report 8 Aug 2023
records.response: The Ministry told CAG in December 2022 that it had taken the matter up with its IEC division. The 2 Apr 2026 parliamentary action-taken report was also reviewed, but concerns recommendations of the Committee’s 9 threport and does not establish reconciliation, delivered-media receipts or recovery for CAG §5.5.1. This absence is not proof that no action exists elsewhere.
alternativeExplanations: Cross-scheme awareness can serve a legitimate public purpose; it still needs a lawful expenditure head and proof of delivery.

records.falsifier: Produce the contemporaneous approved head-change, DAVP invoice and campaign execution certificates, payment ledger and a paragraph-specific accepted action-taken/recovery record.
